clue.text: Forced into improper caress, maiden yells

indicators.note: something forced into a container is pushed inside it, so one piece goes within the other
improper means not as it should be, so these letters are put in another order

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An unwanted embrace leads a young woman to shriek in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improper' rearranges CARESS to SCREAS, and 'Forced into' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are loud cries, so the plural verb and noun are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Notes from instruments at the end of Schubert's First

indicators.note: at the end of says the instruments come after the other piece
First picks out only the opening letter of the composer's name

parts.note: harps are stringed instruments

explanation.surface: Musical notes drawn from instruments at the close of a Schubert symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the end of' places HARPS after S, the first letter of Schubert.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharps are notes raised a semitone, marked with the hash-like musical symbol.

clue.text: Really good person in Oz gets murderer

definitions.meaning: Australian slang for an excellent person or thing
a killer, as in Jack the infamous Victorian killer

explanation.surface: An Australian hero turns out to be a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is Australia; 'gets' just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang praises a great person this way, while it also names a slashing murderer like Jack.

clue.text: Designers given new site chart, about to get stuck in

indicators.note: to get stuck in means to be put inside, so one piece lodges within the other
new says the letters are made into something fresh, a different arrangement

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Planners receive a fresh map of the location and get down to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SITE CHART, and 'to get stuck in' places C (circa) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Architects are the professionals who plan and draw up buildings.

clue.text: Shoe with a nasty smell dumped in street

indicators.note: dumped in means dropped inside, so these letters go within the street abbreviation

parts.note: BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A shoe that reeks has been thrown out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a wooden clog, a heavy shoe carved from one block, worn by French peasants.

clue.text: Mother turning head in rage

indicators.note: turning means the word for mother is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names

explanation.surface: A mother suddenly loses her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses DAM to MAD; NESS is a headland, a sense of 'head' often used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage in the sense of wild fury or frenzy is a synonym of insanity in its older sense.

clue.text: English bishop in silent act with holy books must bring joy

indicators.note: in places the English and bishop letters within the silent performance

parts.note: a mime is a performance without words
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
NT is the New Testament, a set of holy books

explanation.surface: A clergyman's wordless performance with the scriptures should bring happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns describe high spirits, fun and gladness, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Legislative assembly to fade away over time

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: to die away is to fade out

explanation.surface: A parliament gradually loses influence over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Some countries, such as Japan, call their parliament by this name, from Latin dies, a day of meeting.

clue.text: Condition of selfish person with an image somehow restricting love

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the outer letters hold the zero
somehow says the letters are arranged in an unspecified fresh way

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: A self-centred person is obsessed with their image, which keeps out love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges AN IMAGE, and 'restricting' holds O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an obsessive self-absorption, a state a vain, self-centred person suffers from.

clue.text: Bad language — s-in!

parts.note: the letter s is taken as written
to be in a coat is to be wearing it

explanation.surface: Cursing is condemned as sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'sin' as S and IN, then read IN as dressed in a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad language means oaths and profanity, the act of cursing.

clue.text: A flavour slightly lacking in jelly

indicators.note: slightly lacking means missing just a little, here the final letter of the word

parts.note: spice gives food its flavour, so the two can stand for each other

explanation.surface: A dessert jelly tastes rather bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly lacking' drops the last letter of SPICE, leaving SPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Be physically aggressive towards European guide on canal journey?

parts.note: to barge someone is to shove or push into them roughly
a Pole is a native of Poland, so a European

explanation.surface: Someone is rough with a foreigner during a waterway trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whimsical: a long pole pushes and steers a barge, guiding it along the canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pole for pushing a barge along steers the boat, so it can playfully be called its guide.

clue.text: I act with a pride, running round, dealing with sick children

indicators.note: running round suggests the letters circulating and settling in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An actor boasts of performing proudly among a troupe of lions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running round' rearranges the letters of I ACT and A PRIDE together.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the branch of medicine concerned with treating children's illnesses.

clue.text: Quiet atmosphere in match

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for playing quietly
air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture is played in a hushed mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To match two things is to put them together as a couple, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Clear 'hello' unexpected in a place to say 'bonjour'

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters turn up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A cheerful greeting rings out somewhere French.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a port city on the Atlantic coast of France, where people greet you in French.

clue.text: Careful thought shown by journalist backing freedom

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the letters for the journalist are read in reverse

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is a stock crossword journalist
liberation is the act of being set free

explanation.surface: A reporter supports liberty after considering it carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: It means the slow weighing up of a matter before deciding, a near synonym.

clue.text: Any number released from detention in underground operation

indicators.note: released from means let out of, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: internment is detention without trial
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Prisoners are freed from custody in a covert operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial puts the body under the ground, so it is playfully an operation underground.

clue.text: Detestable, like someone on trial right for being locked up

indicators.note: being locked up means held inside, so the letter goes within the defendant

parts.note: the accused is the defendant in a trial

explanation.surface: Hateful, like a defendant hoping to avoid prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cursed is hateful or abominable, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Some stranger in garden is deeply annoying

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An intruder in the garden is highly irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: To anger is to annoy deeply, so the participle form matches the verb phrase.

clue.text: Basic rules for health

definitions.meaning: the founding set of principles by which a state or club is governed
one's physical make-up and robustness, as in a strong or weak body

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a body of founding laws and a person's physical condition.

clue.text: One Catholic left trapped by Anglican church coterie

indicators.note: trapped by means caught inside, so these letters sit within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
I is the Roman numeral one
RC is Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A lone Catholic remains stuck among Anglicans.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a select group of people sharing interests, a social set.

clue.text: Minister given award, no unknown saint

indicators.note: no means without, so the unknown letter is removed

parts.note: a prize is an award
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A clergyman receives an honour but is not considered a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a clergyman, such as one ordained in a church.

clue.text: Exploits and tricks to get rid of king

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: ruses are tricks or stratagems
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone schemes and deceives to topple a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Having more wind? Hardier gut possibly wanted!

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A sufferer from flatulence longs for a tougher stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HARDIER GUT; 'wanted' just completes the joke. The definition plays on wind as digestive gas, though it means breezier.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughty room lets in more currents of air, so the comparative means breezier.

clue.text: Disturbance at university with clique needing to be kept under

indicators.note: in a down clue the clique goes beneath the other piece

parts.note: being up means in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
a set is a clique or group

explanation.surface: A campus fracas involving an elite group must be suppressed.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a disturbance or upheaval, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Bird with other birds heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: auks are sea birds such as razorbills

explanation.surface: A seabird migrates north alongside a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large predatory seabird, an example of the category.

clue.text: Martinets as those who won't give up keeping learner in

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the learner's letter goes within the word

parts.note: stickers are people who stick at a task and persevere
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: Strict disciplinarians are those who persist even with a novice in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian, someone insistent on exact rules and procedure.

clue.text: Money is an attraction ensnaring Charlie

indicators.note: ensnaring means trapping inside, so one piece is caught within the other

parts.note: a lure is something that attracts or entices
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Cash is the bait that traps a man called Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a disparaging word for cash, as in filthy lucre, especially when gained dishonestly.

clue.text: Sort of vehicle one might associate with Rover?

definitions.text: Sort of vehicle one might associate with Rover?

parts.words: Sort of vehicle one might associate with Rover?
parts.note: Rover is a classic dog's name and also a British car make, so a vehicle linked to Rover suggests a cart for a dog

explanation.walkthrough: Rover looks like the British car maker, but here it is a dog's name; a light two-wheeled horse carriage was once named for the dogs carried in it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, originally with a box for carrying sporting dogs.

clue.text: Socialist types in criminal activity stealing French article

indicators.note: stealing here means taking in, so the article is held within the crime

parts.note: theft is a crime of taking property
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Socialists are accused of a crime involving something taken from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Political socialists and progressives are collectively called by this name for one wing of politics.
